processing: Little is documented about how this cultivar is usually made; most Japanese cultivars of this kind are steamed, rolled and dried as sencha.
harvest_season: Spring. Offered at least some of the time as a first shincha picking; the exact timing of the cultivar is poorly documented.
appearance_dry: Typical of sencha: dark green rolled needles.
appearance_wet: Typical of sencha: soft green leaf pieces.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting description is on record for this cultivar; expect the fresh, green character typical of Japanese spring sencha.

brewing.notes: Generic sencha settings, cool enough to keep a shincha sweet. Adjust by taste.

vintage_note: As is usual for Japanese green tea, it would be sold as the current spring harvest, and as shincha when offered as a first picking. Drink it fresh, within about a year.
description:
Shouju (松寿) is a name on lists of Japanese tea cultivars, but very little else is on record about it. It sits at the obscure end of the Japanese tea world.

Without cultivar-specific information, the sensible expectation is ordinary steamed green tea, made like other sencha.

For the same reason there is no trustworthy tasting note. Brew it as you would a shincha, around 70°C with a short steep, and judge it for yourself.

If you meet it, ask the seller where it was grown and how it was made, because the label is likely to be your best information. Do not assume a link to any similarly named tea.
history: Little is documented. The cultivar appears under the name 松寿 in lists of Japanese tea cultivars and has been offered as a first shincha picking, but its breeder, date and parentage are not recorded in accessible references.
